turns.text: Behind the technical name Fast R-CNN, what intuitive problem were researchers confronting?

R-CNN achieved strong detection accuracy but ran a convolutional network independently for thousands of proposed regions. Fast R-CNN reorganized the computation so the expensive convolutional backbone was shared across the whole image.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?
The image is processed once into a feature map, and RoI pooling extracts fixed-size features for each proposal. A single network jointly predicts class probabilities and refined bounding boxes.
Why did the idea outlive one paper or experiment? What did later researchers actually inherit?

Experts generally view Fast R-CNN as the key efficiency bridge between R-CNN and fully integrated proposal networks. Its shared features and joint loss became standard design patterns in two-stage detectors.
Fast R-CNN mattered not only as a result, but as a method that later researchers could test, adapt, and extend.
